segments.text: “When he saw me ruling after having myself crowned king, uncontrollable rage rose in him and he abused me in many ways. I told him what had happened exactly as it had happened. ‘I did this thinking the demon had killed you. I accepted the coronation because the subjects pressed me. This kingdom is yours; take it back. I shall be your servant as before,’ I said, and fell at his feet. But he paid no heed at all to what I said. He thought that, driven by greed, I had sealed the mouth of the cave and unlawfully had myself crowned, and he drove me out of the city. ‘If you come back this way, I will kill you,’ he said, and drove me away. I ran out in the garment I was wearing. From then on I have been wandering in hiding through forests and mountains, keeping myself alive. I have lost everything and am in this state. These four Vanaras alone have remained my companions. Unable, because of anger, to know the truth, my elder brother is committing such injustice. Slay that Vali, that warrior of immense prowess, and save me,”
said Sugriva.

segments.text: Look closely: is there even a drop of truth in Sugriva's words here? Vali goes alone to fight the asura Mayavi. A flood of blood has come surging out of the cave; Sugriva assumes that it is Vali's blood and concludes that he is dead. Both sides are fighting inside the cave. And Sugriva himself knows that Vali is a warrior whom no one can defeat. Achariyar has noted in the 13.3.1955 issue that Sugriva himself tells Rama that Vali was the warrior who, with one blow, felled Dundubhi—the buffalo-shaped asura with the strength of a thousand elephants, whom neither Himavan nor Samudra Raja could defeat—and hurled him beyond a distance of one yojana. Could Sugriva have thought that the blood flowing out belonged to a Vali of such strength?—Very well! Even if he wrongly thought that his elder brother had died, what should the younger brother have done? Should he not have said, ‘What life is there for me after my elder brother is gone?’, gathered his forces, entered the cave with minister Hanuman and confronted Mayavi?—Leaving that aside, what justice was there in placing a huge rock at the mouth of the cave, sealing it and coming away?—Is it not the truth that Sugriva had been waiting for the day Vali would be gone so that he could usurp the kingdom!

Achariyar has noted in the 13.3.1955 issue that Sugriva himself tells Rama that Vali was the warrior who, with one blow, felled Dundubhi—the buffalo-shaped asura with the strength of a thousand elephants, whom neither Himavan nor Samudra Raja could defeat—and hurled him beyond a distance of one yojana. Could Sugriva have thought that the blood flowing out belonged to a Vali of such strength?—Very well! Even if he wrongly thought that his elder brother had died, what should the younger brother have done? Should he not have said, ‘What life is there for me after my elder brother is gone?’, gathered his forces, entered the cave with minister Hanuman and confronted Mayavi?—Leaving that aside, what justice was there in placing a huge rock at the mouth of the cave, sealing it and coming away?—Is it not the truth that Sugriva had been waiting for the day Vali would be gone so that he could usurp the kingdom!

segments.text: If Rama takes as his friend a Sugriva of such deceitful character and with such a heart devoid of affection, what are we to think of Rama's heart? Rama is praised as an elder brother who has Lakshmana, a younger brother of undying affection— then how is it fitting that Rama should seek the aid of the traitor Sugriva, who betrayed his elder brother?—Achariyar alone must explain that. The elder brother and the demon fought, they say. A flood of blood rolled through the cave, they say. Instead of thinking the demon had died, he thought his elder brother had died, they say; to save his own life he sealed the cave, they say. The subjects wanted him to wear the crown, they say! And he wore it, they say! When his elder brother returned, he told him the truth, they say; the elder brother would not listen, they say! After he was caught—after the conspiracy came to light—the traitor staged a sham drama to escape! Rama becomes his ally! Here Achariyar dodges.

segments.text: This is Achariyar's verdict!—If so, should not Rama's course of action have been to make peace between the two brothers and obtain the help of both! But that was not Rama's action! Why? Why, Achariyar; why?

articles.titleEn: Hold Their Feet Until Your Purpose Is Achieved!

segments.text: வாலியின் மார்பில் குத்தி நின்ற பாணத்தை நீலன் மெல்ல அகற்றினான். உடனே காயத்திலிருந்து மலையருவிபோல ரத்தம் பொங்கி, வாலியின் உயிர் உடலைவிட்டுப் பிரிந்தது. அவன் மனைவி தாரை, ‘ஐயோ!’ என அலறி அழுதாள்.
“அங்கதா! உன் தகப்பனைக் கடைசித் தடவையாக வணங்குவாய்!”
என்றாள்.
“உங்களுடைய பிரிய மகன் வணங்கி நிற்கிறானே! அவனுக்கு ஒன்றும் சொல்லமாட்டீர்களா? நான் விதவையானேன். மகனும் திக்கற்றுப் போனான்!”
என்று இதயம் உடைந்த தாரை பிரலாபித்தாள்.

segments.text: இதிலிருந்து விளங்குவது என்ன? சுக்ரீவன் ஆசையின் காரணமாக புத்தி தடுமாறி வாலியை ஒழித்துவிட குகையை மூடினான் என்பதுதான் உண்மையாயிருக்க வேண்டுமென்று நாம் குறிப்பிட்டது சரியாகத் தோன்றுகிறது - இல்லையா? இத்தகைய இழிகுணம் படைத்த சுக்ரீவனுக்குத்தான் துணையாக நின்றான் இராமசந்திர மூர்த்தி என்பதை எண்ணும்போது அவன்பால் எப்படித்தான் பக்தி பிறக்கிறதோ, பூஜனைப்பித்தர்களுக்கு - நாமறியோம்.

என்றல்லவா ராமன் லட்சுமணனிடம் கூறி அனுப்பியிருக்கிறான்!

blocks.text: ராமனுடைய நண்பன் சுக்ரீவன் எத்தகையவன் என்பதை ராமனே விளக்குகிறான் மேற்கண்டவாறு. ராமன் கோபிப்பான் எனக்கண்ட அனுமான், சுக்ரீவனை எச்சரித்து அவனை சீதையைத் தேட அழைக்கிறான். இதற்குள் ராமனுடைய உத்தரவுப்படி லட்சுமணன் கோபாவேசமாகப் பிரவேசிக்கிறான். “உன் அண்ணனை அனுப்பிய இடத்திற்கு உன்னையும் அனுப்புவேன் - என்று சொன்னதாகச் சொல்” என்றல்லவா ராமன் லட்சுமணனிடம் கூறி அனுப்பியிருக்கிறான்!

His wife Tara cried out, “Ayyo!” and wept. “Angada! Bow to your father for the last time!” she said. “Your beloved son stands here bowing! Will you not say anything to him? I have become a widow. The son too has been left without support!” the broken-hearted Tara lamented.

blocks.text: “Was it not because the desire that had hidden within me and worked from inside ruined my reason that, without thinking properly, I sealed the mouth of the cave Vali had entered, seized my elder brother's wealth, and enjoyed it happily?” he began to think to himself. (27.3.1955 — *Kalki*)

segments.text: What becomes clear from this? Does it not seem that what we had pointed out—that Sugriva's reason faltered because of desire and that he sealed the cave in order to get rid of Vali—must indeed be the truth? It was precisely a Sugriva of such base character that Ramachandra Murti stood by— when one thinks of that, how worship-mad people manage to develop devotion toward him—we do not know.

segments.text: “The whole world is full of saundhayam and joy. Sita is suffering somewhere. And I lie here idle, waiting for the favour of an ungrateful Vanara king. This Vanara king, immersed in drink, joining with women and indulging in rustic pleasure, has entirely forgotten the promise he gave me. This Vanara king seems to be a scoundrel.”

Meanwhile, on Rama's orders, Lakshmana enters in a fury. Did Rama not send Lakshmana saying, “Tell him that I will send you too to the place where I sent your elder brother”!

segments.text: And so Lakshmana set out armed and enraged. The Vanaras told Sugriva of Lakshmana's coming and trembled.
“The Vanara king lay intoxicated in the inner palace amid liquor and women. What the Vanaras said did not— enter his ears,”

says Achariyar. Sugriva's negligence turns Lakshmana into a storm. He draws the bowstring and makes it sound. Hearing the resounding sound, Sugriva trembles and sends Tara to speak peace with Lakshmana.

That is why it is also evident that Rama and Lakshmana cultivated friendship with Sugriva—a betrayer of his brother, a scoundrel and an ungrateful man.
